prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 3 columns and 1 row of equal 9:16 panels, 3 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a clean, simple line drawing: uniform thin black outlines on a plain white background, with no shading, hatching, grey tones, colour or texture. Each panel has a thin black border, with plain white gutters between the panels. Location: The Quinn family mansion, living room, Day, soft natural daylight from the tall windows.
Image 1: the character sheet of Natalie (25)
Image 2: the character sheet of Cassie (23)
Image 3: the character sheet of Lauren (50)
Image 4: the location The Quinn family mansion, living room, with no people
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image: the hairstyle, build and outfit in outline. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location image only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location image, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: The camera stays on the near side of the coffee table, facing the back wall, windows at frame left. Natalie stands just inside the right-wall doorway at frame right, beside the empty front-right armchair. Her eyes are closed and wet, with tear-streaked cheeks; the flat hospital statement is at her side and her bag hangs from her shoulder. Cassie stands at the right side of the empty front-left armchair, on the coffee-table side, arms relaxed at her sides. Lauren sits back on the sofa's right end with her legs crossed and her hands still in her lap. George sits on the sofa's left end, staring at the rug; every shot is framed to exclude the sofa's left end, so he stays out of frame.
Panel 1: Medium close-up, eye-level, slow push in from the near side facing the right wall on Natalie by the doorway. Behind her are only the pale grey right wall and the doorway frame; Cassie and the sofa lie beyond frame left. Natalie opens her wet eyes and lifts her chin, tear streaks still on her cheeks. Her gaze is steady and resolved, with no smile.
Panel 2: Close-up, eye-level, locked-off from the near side by the front-right armchair on Cassie beside the front-left armchair. The camera faces the left wall, so behind her the sheer-curtained windows fill the background and the sofa lies beyond frame right. Cassie's glossy pink lips curl into a slow smirk as she looks toward Natalie at frame right.
Panel 3: Medium shot, low angle from the near side facing the back wall on Lauren at the sofa's right end, slight pull out that stops tight on both sides. Behind her are the upper back wall and the potted fig at the right of the arch. The sofa's left end stays beyond frame left and the right-wall doorway with Natalie beyond frame right. Lauren leans back into the sofa and smiles, satisfied, her hands resting still in her lap.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering, shading or colour.
